jobs.description:
CLA is currently seeking a Managing Director – Wealth Strategy & Operations

Why This Role Matters

The next era of Wealth Advisory at CLA is being built right now, and this role will help shape what comes next.

The Managing Director serves as a strategic advisor and operations partner to the Chief Wealth Officer, helping shape and advance the strategic priorities of CLA Wealth Advisory. This leader drives high-impact initiatives involving business transformation, growth, profitability, advisor effectiveness, and organizational scalability. Combining strategic thinking, executive influence, and operational discipline, this role turns complex business challenges into actionable solutions and measurable results.

What Makes The CLA Platform Distinctive

Unlike traditional RIAs, CLA's Wealth Advisory practice one of the nation’s largest wealth management firms operating inside one of the largest accounting firms in the U.S., creating unique opportunities to collaborate across tax, consulting, outsourcing, valuation, and other advisory services while delivering comprehensive solutions to clients. This role will help shape and execute many of the initiatives that define the future of the business.

How Your Strategic Leadership & Execution Is Impactful

Partner closely with the Chief Wealth Officer to evaluate opportunities, solve complex business challenges, and drive the strategic priorities of CLA Wealth Advisory.
Lead complex, cross-functional projects from assessment and recommendation through implementation and adoption that support growth, profitability, and organizational effectiveness.
Develop business cases, financial analyses, and strategic recommendations
Serve as a trusted advisor on issues related to business strategy, operating models, organizational design, client experience, advisor productivity, and growth initiatives.

Business Transformation & Growth

Evaluate opportunities to improve client segmentation, service models, advisor effectiveness, pricing strategies, and operational scalability.
Drive strategic growth, transformation, and acquisition integration efforts across the Wealth business.
Identify opportunities to improve profitability, client outcomes, and advisor experience.

Strategic Leadership & Execution

Lead high-impact strategic initiatives that drive growth, profitability, advisor effectiveness, organizational performance, and long-term scalability across the Wealth business.
Develop business cases, recommendations, and execution plans while influencing and aligning stakeholders across the organization.
Drive accountability, decision-making, and successful execution of complex, cross-functional initiatives, communicating progress and outcomes to executive leadership.

Qualifications

10+ years of relevant experience required
Bachelor's degree required. Combination of relevant experience, education, and training may be accepted in lieu of a degree (Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Economics, or a related field highly preferred).
Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) Series 7, 24, and 65 licenses required (or equivalent). Certified Financial Planner™ (CFP®) designation preferred

Highly Preferred

Leadership experience in Wealth Advisory, wealth management, or financial services, with a demonstrated record of transforming operations, and driving business growth and strategic outcomes highly preferred.

Strong business, financial, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders and drive change across an organization.
Experience within an RIA, wealth management firm, broker-dealer, private wealth platform, or wealth advisory consulting firm; experience with client segmentation, pricing strategy, advisor productivity, and business transformation initiatives required.

Competitive executive compensation and incentive opportunities, comprehensive benefits and retirement programs and Professional growth opportunities within a collaborative, client-focused culture.

jobs.description:
The La Central YMCA is seeking a Program Director.

Job Description

Salary: $66,300 Annually

The YMCA of Greater New York is here for all New Yorkers — to empower youth, improve health, and strengthen community. Founded in 1852, today the Y serves a diverse population of more than half a million New Yorkers who learn, grow, and thrive through programs and services at our 24 branches. Community is the cornerstone of the Y. Together, we connect active, engaged New Yorkers to build stronger communities.

To help fulfill our mission, we cultivate a culture of learning, leading, and collaboration to enhance community impact. Through our talented staff and “LEAP” career framework (Leadership, Empowerment, Accountability, Personal Growth), we are committed to a people-first approach that fosters trust, inclusion, growth, and development for all.

Being part of the YMCA Afterschool staff team is a deeply rewarding job where you support children’s learning, help build strong connections, and have a positive impact on so many in your community. At Y Afterschool, we will create a safe and fun space for kids to learn and grow, lead creative activities, and help them develop valuable skills. This is an opportunity to make a real difference and gain invaluable leadership and interpersonal experience.

The La Central YMCA is seeking a Program Director. Under the supervision of the Youth & Family Director, the Program Director serves as the strategic and operational leader for our Afterschool initiative. This multifaceted role requires a dynamic professional capable of managing all aspects of a successful, holistic youth development program.

Team Leadership: Supervising, mentoring, and leading a diverse staff team to deliver high-quality programming.

Program Excellence: Designing, creating, and implementing engaging and impactful programming that meets the developmental needs of all participants.

Inclusion and Mental Wellness: Prioritizing and integrating mental health support, case management, and social-emotional learning initiatives for both program participants and staff. Ensuring programming and day-to-day operations are welcoming to children of all abilities.

Operational Management: Meticulously managing site budgets, ensuring fiscal responsibility, and maintaining compliance with all contractual agreements and reporting requirements.

Benefits

The YMCA of Greater New York offers a variety of benefits to its staff members, including retirement benefits, medical, paid time off, free YMCA membership, and more! Benefit eligibility is determined by an individual’s employment status (i.e., full-time or part-time), tenure, and/or the number of hours scheduled to work. Click here for more information.

How To Apply

If you would like to be a member of our dynamic team, please complete our online application and submit your résumé and a thoughtful cover letter that explains your interest in the role and our organization.

Qualifications

Must have one (1) of the following:
Associate’s Degree in Child Development, Elementary Education, Physical Education, Recreation, or a related field;
A New York State Children’s Program Administrator Credential;
A School-Age Child Care Credential or other Office-recognized credential specific to the school-age developmental period;
Two (2) years of college with 18 credits in Child Development, Elementary Education, Physical Education, Recreation, or a related field.

Minimum of two (2) years of direct experience working with children under the age of 13.
Minimum of one (1) year of experience in a supervisory capacity in a childcare program or related field of work. Current Pediatrics CPR or First Aid certification preferred.
General knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Strong interpersonal skills, leadership qualities, and comfortable working with diverse youth and adults.

Essential Functions

Direct programs serving the designated grade level band (K-5 or 6-8), ensuring all activities and services are age-appropriate and aligned with DYCD program requirements.
Ensure programs and services are deeply integrated into the specific community we serve and meet the diverse needs of all community members.
Develop and execute effective strategies for recruiting and retaining participants, aiming for consistently high attendance rates and sustained program engagement.
Develop and utilize quantitative measures, quality monitoring tools, and external evaluations to demonstrate program effectiveness.
Routinely analyze data and assessment results to identify trends, measure outcomes, and implement adjustments designed to continuously improve program quality and meet or exceed all established program goals.
Successfully establish, maintain, and leverage connections with local community partners, public/private funders, and external evaluators to enhance program services, increase resource availability, and ensure sustained program success.
Foster and lead staff in the implementation of comprehensive mental wellness support for both participants and families. Provide mental wellness resources to kids and families, and ensure staff are well-trained to create a supportive environment and identify participants who may benefit from mental wellness support/referrals.
Coordinate and implement a crisis plan to support various participant/family needs in conjunction with NYCPS school social workers, mental health staff, and external behavioral health providers.
Oversee the selection of an evidence-based SEL curriculum that is adaptable to a dynamic after-school setting (COMPASS Elementary or SONYC). Ensure all SEL programming is deliberate and clearly defines the specific social and emotional competencies that staff seek to develop in participants.
Manage the program budget, order all supplies in a timely manner, and track all expenses using the tools provided.
Recruit and retain a strong staff team with diverse abilities and backgrounds. Team skills and schedules must ensure that all aspects of the COMPASS program are delivered with an outstanding level of program quality.
Cultivate and maintain strong, collaborative working relationships with host school administration and staff.
Proactively coordinate and discuss planned activity schedules, particularly those related to STEAM and Literacy initiatives, to ensure alignment and integration with the host school's academic goals.
Maintain accurate program documentation as required by the Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS), Department of Health (DOH), Department of Youth & Community Development (DYCD), and YMCA of Greater New York.
Understand and communicate the YMCA’s core values and the goals of the Y Afterschool Program to participants and caregivers.
Develop and maintain positive relationships with parents/guardians and caregivers through regular communication regarding their child’s strengths and areas for growth. Manage communications regarding injuries or incidents, as needed.
Actively participate in training sessions, designated meetings, and special events.
Adhere to all Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS), Department of Health (DOH), YMCA of Greater New York, school partner, and funder standards, expectations, and regulations.

jobs.description:
Position Overview

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as CFSJ’s chief executive and principal ambassador. The Executive Director will provide the vision, leadership, and energy necessary to strengthen the Foundation as a trusted philanthropic partner throughout South Jersey.

This is a highly relational, externally facing leadership role. The Executive Director will be responsible for growing philanthropic assets and individual giving; cultivating donors, fundholders, professional advisors, institutional funders, businesses, and community partners; advancing meaningful community impact; and elevating CFSJ’s profile throughout the region.

At the same time, the Executive Director will lead a small organization through an important period of organizational development. The successful candidate will establish clear priorities and measures of success, build a collaborative and accountable culture, strengthen staff capacity, and work closely with the Board to determine and execute the Foundation’s long-term strategic direction.

The Executive Director will also help the Board assess the opportunities, requirements, and economics associated with potential independence from the Community Foundation of New Jersey and, if that path is chosen, lead the organization through the transition.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership & Organizational Development

Partner with the Board to define and implement a clear, compelling strategic vision for CFSJ and translate that vision into measurable goals and priorities.
Clarify the Foundation’s identity, value proposition, and role within the South Jersey philanthropic ecosystem.
Lead organizational development, including staffing, systems, infrastructure, technology, communications, and operational sustainability.
Establish a culture that is collaborative, accountable, inclusive, energetic, and supportive.
Provide the Board with clear recommendations, regular progress reports, and meaningful measures of organizational performance.
Lead, develop, and grow the CFSJ team, building the capacity, talent, and organizational culture needed to achieve the Foundation’s strategic goals and sustain its growth.

Philanthropic Growth & Donor Engagement

Make philanthropic growth a central leadership priority, with a particular emphasis on expanding individual and family philanthropy throughout South Jersey.
Cultivate and steward major donors, fundholders, families of means, corporations, foundations, and professional advisors.
Develop strategies for major gifts, planned giving, legacy giving, endowment development, donor-advised funds, and other charitable vehicles.
Build a compelling case for CFSJ that connects donors to the needs and opportunities of South Jersey.
Engage the Board as an active partner in donor cultivation, introductions, solicitation, and stewardship.
Diversify the Foundation’s philanthropic base and reduce concentration risk.

Community Leadership & Impact

Serve as a visible and credible champion for South Jersey and for philanthropy throughout the region.
Build authentic relationships with nonprofit leaders, civic leaders, businesses, elected officials, funders, community organizations, and residents.
Listen deeply to communities across all eight counties and ensure CFSJ’s work reflects their needs and aspirations.
Identify opportunities for collaborative initiatives, community investment, and innovative approaches to regional challenges.
Strengthen and communicate CFSJ’s community impact, including the lessons and opportunities emerging from initiatives such as the Camden Food Fund and South Jersey Resiliency Fund.

Board Partnership & Governance

Build a transparent, trusting, and reciprocal partnership with the Board.
Help the Board understand its role as a governing and philanthropic body and provide clear opportunities for members to contribute their time, expertise, relationships, and resources.
Strengthen Board engagement, geographic representation, and effectiveness over time.
Ensure appropriate governance, financial oversight, compliance, and risk management.

Potential Independence & Organizational Transition

Work with the Board to evaluate the strategic, financial, operational, and community implications of independence from the Community Foundation of New Jersey.
If independence is pursued, lead the development of the systems, infrastructure, staffing, financial model, and partnerships required for a sustainable transition.
Maintain a strong relationship with the Community Foundation of New Jersey during any transition.

The Leader:

The ideal candidate will be a relationship-driven, entrepreneurial, and community-minded leader who combines the strategic perspective of a chief executive with the energy and personal engagement of a successful fundraiser and ambassador.

The next Executive Director will be a builder, someone who can strengthen what already exists while bringing fresh thinking, greater visibility, and new energy to the organization. They will be comfortable operating in a small organization where leadership is highly hands-on and where success depends upon the ability to move fluidly between strategy, fundraising, community engagement, staff leadership, and execution.

The successful candidate will bring many of the following qualifications and attributes:

Significant senior leadership experience in a community foundation, philanthropic institution, nonprofit organization, or related social-sector environment.
Demonstrated success in fundraising, donor cultivation, major gifts, or philanthropic asset development.
Strong understanding of community foundations, charitable giving vehicles, and the role of philanthropy in community development.
Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, with the ability to connect authentically with individuals from diverse backgrounds and across different sectors.
Credibility and comfort with high-net-worth individuals, families, professional advisors, institutional funders, corporate leaders, and community stakeholders.
A strong personal connection to South Jersey—or the demonstrated ability and commitment to become deeply embedded in the region and understand its distinctive communities.
Strategic vision coupled with a strong bias toward action, accountability, and measurable results.
Experience leading, developing, and motivating staff, ideally in a small or entrepreneurial organization.
The ability to build trust through transparency, candor, accessibility, and follow-through.
Strong financial and organizational acumen, including experience overseeing budgets and organizational resources.
Comfort with technology, data, CRM systems, and the use of information to support decision-making and donor relationships.
A collaborative leadership style and the confidence to make decisions, provide direction, and respectfully challenge assumptions when appropriate.
An appreciation for the diversity of South Jersey and a demonstrated commitment to equity, inclusion, and community voice.

Most importantly, the successful candidate will be a connector and storyteller, someone who can articulate why South Jersey matters, why philanthropy matters, and why CFSJ is uniquely positioned to make a difference.

Education:

A bachelor’s degree is preferred, although substantial relevant professional experience and demonstrated leadership achievement will be considered in lieu of a traditional academic credential

Location:

The Community Foundation of South Jersey operates as a remote organization. The Executive Director is expected to be highly visible and regularly present throughout the eight-county region, with frequent in-person engagement with donors, fundholders, nonprofit and civic partners, Board members, and community leaders.

Given the highly relationship-driven nature of the position, candidates should expect significant travel throughout South Jersey and an active presence in the communities CFSJ serves.

Compensation:

The anticipated salary range for this position is $160,000–$190,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications. A competitive benefits package will also be provided.

Closing Perspective

This is an opportunity to lead an organization with meaningful assets, strong community roots, and significant untapped potential at a pivotal moment in its history.

The next Executive Director will not simply inherit an established institution. They will help shape what CFSJ becomes.

Success will mean a Foundation with a clear identity and strategy; a broader and more diverse base of donors and fundholders; stronger relationships throughout all eight counties; meaningful and visible community impact; an engaged and effective Board; an energized staff; and a sustainable organizational model positioned for the future.

For the right leader, this is an opportunity to become a highly visible champion for South Jersey and to build an institution that can have lasting philanthropic and community impact across the region.

Position Overview

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as CFSJ’s chief executive and principal ambassador. The Executive Director will provide the vision, leadership, and energy necessary to strengthen the Foundation as a trusted philanthropic partner throughout South Jersey.

This is a highly relational, externally facing leadership role. The Executive Director will be responsible for growing philanthropic assets and individual giving; cultivating donors, fundholders, professional advisors, institutional funders, businesses, and community partners; advancing meaningful community impact; and elevating CFSJ’s profile throughout the region.

At the same time, the Executive Director will lead a small organization through an important period of organizational development. The successful candidate will establish clear priorities and measures of success, build a collaborative and accountable culture, strengthen staff capacity, and work closely with the Board to determine and execute the Foundation’s long-term strategic direction.

The Executive Director will also help the Board assess the opportunities, requirements, and economics associated with potential independence from the Community Foundation of New Jersey and, if that path is chosen, lead the organization through the transition.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership & Organizational Development

Partner with the Board to define and implement a clear, compelling strategic vision for CFSJ and translate that vision into measurable goals and priorities.
Clarify the Foundation’s identity, value proposition, and role within the South Jersey philanthropic ecosystem.
Lead organizational development, including staffing, systems, infrastructure, technology, communications, and operational sustainability.
Establish a culture that is collaborative, accountable, inclusive, energetic, and supportive.
Provide the Board with clear recommendations, regular progress reports, and meaningful measures of organizational performance.
Lead, develop, and grow the CFSJ team, building the capacity, talent, and organizational culture needed to achieve the Foundation’s strategic goals and sustain its growth.

Philanthropic Growth & Donor Engagement

Make philanthropic growth a central leadership priority, with a particular emphasis on expanding individual and family philanthropy throughout South Jersey.
Cultivate and steward major donors, fundholders, families of means, corporations, foundations, and professional advisors.
Develop strategies for major gifts, planned giving, legacy giving, endowment development, donor-advised funds, and other charitable vehicles.
Build a compelling case for CFSJ that connects donors to the needs and opportunities of South Jersey.
Engage the Board as an active partner in donor cultivation, introductions, solicitation, and stewardship.
Diversify the Foundation’s philanthropic base and reduce concentration risk.

Community Leadership & Impact

Serve as a visible and credible champion for South Jersey and for philanthropy throughout the region.
Build authentic relationships with nonprofit leaders, civic leaders, businesses, elected officials, funders, community organizations, and residents.
Listen deeply to communities across all eight counties and ensure CFSJ’s work reflects their needs and aspirations.
Identify opportunities for collaborative initiatives, community investment, and innovative approaches to regional challenges.
Strengthen and communicate CFSJ’s community impact, including the lessons and opportunities emerging from initiatives such as the Camden Food Fund and South Jersey Resiliency Fund.

Board Partnership & Governance

Build a transparent, trusting, and reciprocal partnership with the Board.
Help the Board understand its role as a governing and philanthropic body and provide clear opportunities for members to contribute their time, expertise, relationships, and resources.
Strengthen Board engagement, geographic representation, and effectiveness over time.
Ensure appropriate governance, financial oversight, compliance, and risk management.

Potential Independence & Organizational Transition

Work with the Board to evaluate the strategic, financial, operational, and community implications of independence from the Community Foundation of New Jersey.
If independence is pursued, lead the development of the systems, infrastructure, staffing, financial model, and partnerships required for a sustainable transition.
Maintain a strong relationship with the Community Foundation of New Jersey during any transition.

The Leader:

The ideal candidate will be a relationship-driven, entrepreneurial, and community-minded leader who combines the strategic perspective of a chief executive with the energy and personal engagement of a successful fundraiser and ambassador.

The next Executive Director will be a builder, someone who can strengthen what already exists while bringing fresh thinking, greater visibility, and new energy to the organization. They will be comfortable operating in a small organization where leadership is highly hands-on and where success depends upon the ability to move fluidly between strategy, fundraising, community engagement, staff leadership, and execution.

The successful candidate will bring many of the following qualifications and attributes:

Significant senior leadership experience in a community foundation, philanthropic institution, nonprofit organization, or related social-sector environment.
Demonstrated success in fundraising, donor cultivation, major gifts, or philanthropic asset development.
Strong understanding of community foundations, charitable giving vehicles, and the role of philanthropy in community development.
Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, with the ability to connect authentically with individuals from diverse backgrounds and across different sectors.
Credibility and comfort with high-net-worth individuals, families, professional advisors, institutional funders, corporate leaders, and community stakeholders.
A strong personal connection to South Jersey—or the demonstrated ability and commitment to become deeply embedded in the region and understand its distinctive communities.
Strategic vision coupled with a strong bias toward action, accountability, and measurable results.
Experience leading, developing, and motivating staff, ideally in a small or entrepreneurial organization.
The ability to build trust through transparency, candor, accessibility, and follow-through.
Strong financial and organizational acumen, including experience overseeing budgets and organizational resources.
Comfort with technology, data, CRM systems, and the use of information to support decision-making and donor relationships.
A collaborative leadership style and the confidence to make decisions, provide direction, and respectfully challenge assumptions when appropriate.
An appreciation for the diversity of South Jersey and a demonstrated commitment to equity, inclusion, and community voice.

Most importantly, the successful candidate will be a connector and storyteller, someone who can articulate why South Jersey matters, why philanthropy matters, and why CFSJ is uniquely positioned to make a difference.

Education:

A bachelor’s degree is preferred, although substantial relevant professional experience and demonstrated leadership achievement will be considered in lieu of a traditional academic credential

Location:

The Community Foundation of South Jersey operates as a remote organization. The Executive Director is expected to be highly visible and regularly present throughout the eight-county region, with frequent in-person engagement with donors, fundholders, nonprofit and civic partners, Board members, and community leaders.

Given the highly relationship-driven nature of the position, candidates should expect significant travel throughout South Jersey and an active presence in the communities CFSJ serves.

Compensation:

The anticipated salary range for this position is $160,000–$190,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications. A competitive benefits package will also be provided.

Closing Perspective

This is an opportunity to lead an organization with meaningful assets, strong community roots, and significant untapped potential at a pivotal moment in its history.

The next Executive Director will not simply inherit an established institution. They will help shape what CFSJ becomes.

Success will mean a Foundation with a clear identity and strategy; a broader and more diverse base of donors and fundholders; stronger relationships throughout all eight counties; meaningful and visible community impact; an engaged and effective Board; an energized staff; and a sustainable organizational model positioned for the future.

For the right leader, this is an opportunity to become a highly visible champion for South Jersey and to build an institution that can have lasting philanthropic and community impact across the region.
